children.text: Throughout the entire video, Noel relies on key platform affordances, using clean visual editing and concise onscreen text overlays to emphasize his most important words. By maintaining a simple setup with no distracting objects in the background, just a direct-to-camera shot without any flashy edits or aggressive sales plugs, he leverages Instagram’s video format to create an authentic, face-to-face atmosphere, making the viewer feel more welcome. This deliberate visual restraint prevents the video from feeling commercialized and fake, allowing the serious mood of Men’s Mental Health Month to take center stage. The minimalistic production style strengthens his emotional appeal by making the interaction feel like an honest, personal conversation, such as one you would have with a friend.

Noel opens the video with a serious tone, talking about how he almost ended his life when he was in his 20s. Through the affordance of the text caption, “I nearly offed myself” can be seen, which carries a certain weight and disturbance with it. The fact that the word “killed,” and that Noel must mold his sentence to avoid directly saying that he almost committed suicide are just two sick examples of the language constraint that is enforced by Instagram. To bypass getting shadow banned or having his content removed due to platform guidelines, he adopts filtered internet slang while still maintaining his emotional vulnerability to build immediate rapport with his followers and any new viewers that may come along.

Noel shifts the focus away from his personal struggles onto his target audience: the young men and gym-goers that are actively navigating intense social and societal pressures. By directly addressing his viewers with direct eye contact with the camera and empathetic language, Noel manages to create a safe space that sharply contrasts with the typical hyper-masculine gym culture. This segment relies a lot on appealing to his audience’s emotions, validating their suppressed emotions and mental health struggles. Instead of speaking as an untouchable fitness authority, he is positioning himself as a relatable peer, a wise mentor, who understands their quiet battles, encouraging his followers to break the silence surrounding men’s emotional wellbeing.

Continuing his message, Noel addresses the broader cultural constraints that discourage men from showing vulnerability or seeking professional, or any kind of, help. He uses logical reasoning to challenge the false narrative that staying silent means staying strong, "I'd lie to those around me, telling them that I was okay when I wasn't." By sharing his own past rock-bottom moments, he argues that acknowledging depression or suicidal thoughts is a vital step towards healing rather than a sign of personal failure. This rhetorical appeal explicitly targets society’s expectations of hyper-masculinity, reassuring his audience that prioritizing their mental health does not diminish their physical strength or manhood; they stand nothing to lose and everything to gain.

Noel's primary purpose throughout this reel is to destigmatize mental health struggles among young men whilst providing a message of hope and survival to men of all ages. By combining his personal account of overcoming depression, where he nearly gave in multiple times, with an explicit call to action during Men's Mental Health Month, he aims to shift fitness culture away from pure aesthetic obsession towards overall well-being, physical and mental. He utilizes a balance of vulnerability and wisdom to convince his audience that reaching out for help is a sign of strength, a polar opposite of what has been instilled in them over their lifetimes. Ultimately, his goal extends beyond entertainment or promoting his brands and sponsors; he seeks to save lives by normalizing emotional transparency.

This video operates within the fitness influencer content genre, specifically within Instagram, but Noel deliberately subverts traditional expectations of those sorts of reels. Typical fitness reels prioritize unrealistic body types, intense training regiments and diets, or commercial product placements. In contrast, Noel adopts a hybrid genre format within this video, blending in an intimate confession with a formal public service announcement. Since Noel regularly trains, he retains the visual identity of a bodybuilder, so while he is delivering a somber, empathetic monologue, the target audience, young men, tend to pay more attention. Overall, this genre shift surprises the viewer scrolling through standard workout content, making his tone and serious message stand out sharply against typical algorithmic slop.
